stem: In a quality check, each unit has a 20% chance of being defective, independent of others. A batch of 5 units is inspected. What is the probability that at most 1 unit is defective? [Given: (0.8)^5 = 0.32768, (0.8)^4 = 0.4096]

per_option_rationale.rationale: 0.32768 = P(X=0) only; the student solved for exactly 0 defectives instead of at most 1.
0.40960 = P(X=1) only; the student solved for exactly 1 defective instead of at most 1.
0.67232 = 1 - P(X=0) = 1 - 0.32768, which is P(X>=1), i.e. the complement of zero defectives rather than P(X<=1).

explanation_sections.punchline: At most 1 requires summing two terms: P(X=0) and P(X=1), not just one.
explanation_sections.lesson: At most k always means summing from 0 to k; do not stop at P(X=0) for at-most-1 questions.
explanation_sections.timing: 75 seconds. Use the given hints for (0.8)^5 and (0.8)^4; avoid recalculating powers. Trap: picking 0.32768 alone.
